results.content: Annual inflation in the euro zone rose to 3.8% in September, beating market expectations to hit its highest level since September 2023. Last month's print is up from the 3.2% recorded in August, above the 3.6% forecast by markets and well ahead of the European Central Bank's 2% target. Core inflation came in at 2.5%, in line with expectations. The move was fueled by soaring energy prices caused by the ongoing Middle East conflict. This is a developing story.
results.title: Eurozone inflation hits its highest level in three years at 3.8% - CNBC

results.content: U.S. consumer sentiment dipped to a four-month low in September amid rising inflation rates and mounting cost-of-living concerns, according to survey results released Friday. The University of Michigan Surveys of Consumers index found that consumer confidence slipped to a reading of 48.1 in September, a 7 percent decrease from August and 15 percent less than in January. Republican sentiment in September is 20 percent lower than in January, while Democrats are down 13 percent over the same period, according to the survey. results.content: Nearly two thirds of family offices cited inflation as their top investing concern, according to a new report from Citi Wealth. However, investment firms of the ultra-wealthy are still prioritizing growth with plans to increase allocations to public equities, private equity and direct investments over the next 12 months, per the findings. In the annual survey of 351 firms conducted in June and July, 63% of respondents selected inflation as their top concern, up from 37% in 2025. Looking forward, nearly a third of respondents, on net, said they planned to increase their exposure to global developed equities over the next 12 months. results.content: US consumer sentiment fell to its second-lowest level on record in September as high gas prices further soured Americans’ views of the economy. The University of Michigan’s consumer sentiment index for September dipped to 48.1, notching a 7% decline from August and a nearly 13% drop from a year ago, according to data released Friday. After navigating a once-in-a-century global pandemic, US households have had to contend with higher-than-normal inflation – and the compounding effects of fast-rising prices – for the past five and a half years.
